study_context.outcome: Alive and independent (Oxford Handicap Score 0-2) at 6 months
study_context.population: Acute ischemic stroke patients within 6 hours of symptom onset

hypothesis.title: AF-Infarct Type Conflict
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: The presence of Atrial Fibrillation combined with evidence of early infarct on CT significantly reduces the window of benefit for alteplase.

treatment_recommendation.rationale: 32% of difficult samples have AF and 40% have early infarct signs. This combination suggests large-artery cardioembolic strokes that have already transitioned to irreversible injury.

hypothesis.mechanism: Cardioembolic clots are often larger and more organized; if early infarct signs are present, the tissue is highly susceptible to bleeding upon reperfusion.
evidence_basis: Infarct feature mean is 0.40 in failure cases
Atrialfib_rand mean is 0.32 in failure cases
hypothesis.testable_prediction: The combination of AF and visible infarct on baseline CT will be the strongest predictor of treatment failure in the 3-6 hour window.

hypothesis.title: Consciousness Level as a Proxy for Collateral Failure
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: Patients with a 'normal' GCS but moderate NIHSS represent a specific failure group where collateral circulation is failing despite preserved consciousness.

treatment_recommendation.rationale: Difficult samples often have high GCS (median 0.757) but ended in failure. These patients need more aggressive secondary neuroprotection alongside alteplase.

hypothesis.mechanism: Preserved GCS masks the severity of focal ischemia, leading to delayed treatment or underestimation of the penumbral volume that is at risk of 'sink-effect' post-lysis.
evidence_basis: GCS score median is 0.757 (high/normal) in difficult cases
Stroketype 1.0 and 2.0 (Total/Partial anterior circulation) comprise 92% of failure cases
hypothesis.testable_prediction: Patients with GCS 15 but NIHSS > 10 will have higher rates of 'malignant' edema regardless of alteplase treatment.

hypothesis.title: Female Cardioembolic Resistance Interaction
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: Elderly female patients with atrial fibrillation and low NIHSS are more likely to have poor outcomes despite treatment due to higher hemorrhagic transformation risk or non-salvageable tissue.

treatment_recommendation.rationale: 64% of difficult samples are female, with 32% having atrial fibrillation. The combination increases risk of large-vessel occlusion which respond poorly to IV lysis alone.

hypothesis.mechanism: Cardioembolic strokes in females often involve larger clots (AFib source) and higher vascular fragility, leading to a narrower therapeutic window for thrombolysis where the risk of hemorrhage outweighs the benefit of late recanalization.
evidence_basis: High prevalence of gender=1.0 and atrialfib_rand=1.0 in difficult-to-predict cases.
hypothesis.testable_prediction: Female patients with AFib will show a statistically significant increase in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage compared to males with AFib when treated with rt-PA.

hypothesis.title: Age and Neuroplasticity
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: The treatment effect of IV alteplase on 6-month independence is greater in patients aged < 70 compared to older patients.

treatment_recommendation.rationale: Younger patients have better baseline neuroplasticity and lower risk of hemorrhagic transformation, leading to more robust recovery after successful recanalization.

hypothesis.mechanism: Higher vascular integrity and lower burden of small vessel disease in younger patients reduces the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage.
evidence_basis: NINDS trial post-hoc analysis
SITS-MOST registry data
hypothesis.testable_prediction: Significant interaction between age and treatment; OHS 0-2 odds ratio > 1.2 in age < 70 subgroup.

hypothesis.title: Glucose-Mediated Penumbra Toxicity
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: Baseline hyperglycemia (glucose > 8.0 mmol/L) reduces the probability of a positive outcome with alteplase due to increased oxidative stress.

treatment_recommendation.rationale: Hyperglycemia promotes anaerobic metabolism in the ischemic penumbra, accelerating tissue death and increasing blood-brain barrier permeability.

hypothesis.mechanism: Lactic acidosis and matrix metalloproteinase activation under hyperglycemic conditions exacerbate reperfusion injury.
evidence_basis: EPITHET study results
WAKE-UP trial observations
hypothesis.testable_prediction: Treatment effect on OHS 0-2 will be significantly smaller in the glucose > 8.0 group compared to lower glucose levels.

hypothesis.title: Severity-Dependent Benefit (NIHSS)
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: Patients with moderate stroke severity (NIHSS 5-15) derive the greatest benefit from alteplase.

treatment_recommendation.rationale: Moderate severity strokes often have salvageable penumbra, whereas very severe strokes (NIHSS > 15) may have large established cores and high hemorrhage risk.

hypothesis.mechanism: Optimal balance between salvageable tissue volume and the risk of large-volume hemorrhagic transformation.
evidence_basis: Cochrane review on thrombolysis
IST-3 primary paper
hypothesis.testable_prediction: Interaction between NIHSS and treatment; maximal absolute risk reduction in the 5-15 score range.

hypothesis.title: Blood Pressure and Hemorrhage Risk
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: High systolic blood pressure (SBP > 160 mmHg) at presentation increases the risk of harm from alteplase.

subgroup_rule.description: Systolic blood pressure above 160 mmHg at randomization

treatment_recommendation.rationale: Elevated blood pressure following thrombolysis is the strongest predictor of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage.

hypothesis.mechanism: Hypertensive stress on the reperfused microvasculature causes vessel rupture in the setting of tPA-induced fibrinogenolysis.
evidence_basis: SITS-ISTR registry data
AHA Stroke Guidelines
hypothesis.testable_prediction: Increased rate of poor OHS outcomes in the treated group specifically when sbprand > 160.

hypothesis.title: Hypotensive Hypoperfusion Limitation
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: Lower systolic and diastolic blood pressure at presentation in the presence of moderate NIHSS scores predicts failure of rt-PA due to insufficient collateral flow to maintain penumbra.

subgroup_rule.description: Systolic BP below the mean of difficult samples

treatment_recommendation.rationale: Difficult samples show lower than average SBP and DBP, suggesting that thrombolysis cannot save tissue if perfusion pressure is already compromised.

hypothesis.mechanism: Low systemic blood pressure reduces collateral circulation to the ischemic penumbra. Even if rt-PA achieves recanalization, the delay and prior period of profound hypoperfusion result in completed infarction before reperfusion is achieved.
evidence_basis: Mean sbprand of -0.146 and mean dbprand of -0.068 in difficult cases.
hypothesis.testable_prediction: A positive correlation will exist between higher SBP (within safety limits) and successfully salvaged penumbra volume on CT perfusion.

hypothesis.title: Antiplatelet-Mediated Lysis Resistance
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: Patients previously on antiplatelet therapy who present with minor stroke (Stroketype 2.0) derive less benefit from rt-PA due to altered clot architecture and increased bleeding risk.

treatment_recommendation.rationale: 56% of failed predictions occurred in patients on antiplatelets, particularly clustered with high weight and lower GCS.

hypothesis.mechanism: Pre-existing antiplatelet therapy alters the fibrin structure and increases the risk of microvascular leakage. In minor strokes, the potential benefit of lysis is small compared to the increased risk of hemorrhagic conversion in these patients.
evidence_basis: Antiplat_rand mean of 0.56 in difficult samples vs expectations.
hypothesis.testable_prediction: Pre-treated antiplatelet patients will have higher Oxford Handicap Scores at 6 months compared to antiplatelet-naive patients with similar NIHSS.

hypothesis.title: Low NIHSS and Blood Pressure Fragility
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: In patients with relatively mild stroke (low NIHSS), even moderate systolic blood pressure elevation leads to poor outcomes due to reperfusion injury.

subgroup_rule.description: Patients with NIHSS below the mean of failure cases

treatment_recommendation.rationale: Difficult samples show a pattern of lower NIHSS (mean -0.198) where the risk of alteplase-induced hemorrhage outweighs the benefit of treating a small occlusion.

hypothesis.mechanism: In low-severity strokes, the penumbra is smaller; alteplase-induced lysis can cause 'luxury perfusion' and hemorrhagic transformation in fragile capillary beds.
evidence_basis: NIHSS mean is negative (-0.198) in difficult samples
Median SBP is relatively low (-0.374), suggesting even normal-range SBP might be problematic in this subgroup
hypothesis.testable_prediction: Patients with NIHSS < 5 will show a higher odds ratio for HT (hemorrhagic transformation) than for 6-month independence.

hypothesis.title: Hyperglycemic-High Weight Resistance
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: Patients with high body weight and elevated blood glucose exhibit a diminished response to standard dose IV alteplase due to relative under-dosing and impaired clot lysis.

subgroup_rule.description: Patients with weight above the mean of difficult samples

treatment_recommendation.rationale: Difficult cases show higher mean weight (0.279) and high glucose variance, suggesting these factors combined with standard fixed-cap dosing limit rt-PA efficacy.

hypothesis.mechanism: High weight leads to reaching the 90mg maximum rt-PA dose earlier, resulting in lower mg/kg delivery. Concurrent hyperglycemia promotes a pro-thrombotic state and strengthens fibrin cross-linking, making these lower-concentration doses ineffective.
evidence_basis: Observed mean weight of 0.279 and max glucose of 4.77 in difficult samples
hypothesis.testable_prediction: Patients in this weight/glucose subgroup will show higher rates of incomplete recanalization on follow-up imaging compared to normal weight/euglycemic patients.

hypothesis.title: Metabolic Threshold for Reperfusion Efficiency
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: Patients with higher body weight and significantly elevated glucose levels exhibit diminished recovery post-alteplase due to a pro-thrombotic state that resists fibrinolysis.

subgroup_rule.description: Patients with weight above the mean of difficult samples

treatment_recommendation.rationale: High body weight combined with glucose variability (seen in difficult samples) suggests a metabolic environment where alteplase increases hemorrhage risk without achieving meaningful recanalization.

hypothesis.mechanism: Adiposity and hyperglycemia increase plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1) levels, leading to 'alteplase resistance' and secondary microvascular injury.
evidence_basis: Weight mean is 0.279 in difficult samples compared to general population
Glucose max reaches 4.77 in failure cases
Higher BMI is associated with baseline fibrinolytic resistance
hypothesis.testable_prediction: Patients in the top quartile of weight and glucose will show higher rates of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and lower 6-month independence.

hypothesis.title: Neurological Dissociation Refractivity
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: Patients with high NIHSS but relatively preserved GCS (indicative of specific lacunar or minor stroke syndromes) are poorly served by standard alteplase protocols.

subgroup_rule.description: GCS at the maximum/median of the difficult samples

treatment_recommendation.rationale: A dissociation between motor deficits (NIHSS) and consciousness (GCS) suggests specific stroke types (like Stroketype 1.0/2.0) that respond heterogeneously.

hypothesis.mechanism: Dissociation between GCS and NIHSS often indicates subcortical or lacunar infarctions where white matter tracts are affected but global brain function is preserved. These clots are often smaller or myogenic, making fibrinolytic response variable.
evidence_basis: GCS score median of 0.75 and NIHSS median of -0.46 in difficult samples.
hypothesis.testable_prediction: The NIHSS-to-GCS ratio will be a better predictor of 6-month independence than either score alone.

hypothesis.title: Gender-Specific Antiplatelet Interference
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: The efficacy of alteplase is reduced in female patients (gender=1.0) who were already on antiplatelet therapy at the time of stroke.

treatment_recommendation.rationale: The high prevalence of pre-stroke antiplatelet use (56%) and females (64%) in difficult samples suggests an interaction that limits the benefit of IV rtPA.

hypothesis.mechanism: Pre-treatment with antiplatelets in women may lead to a different clot composition (platelet-rich) that is less susceptible to thrombolysis compared to fibrin-rich clots.
evidence_basis: Gender mean of 0.64 in difficult samples
Antiplatelet use mean of 0.56 in failure cases
hypothesis.testable_prediction: Females on aspirin will have lower recanalization rates on follow-up imaging compared to males on aspirin when treated with alteplase.

hypothesis.title: Pre-existing Atrial Fibrillation and Thrombus Composition
hypothesis.hypothesis_statement: Alteplase is less effective in patients with pre-existing atrial fibrillation (AF) due to different clot morphology.

subgroup_rule.description: Presence of atrial fibrillation at randomization

treatment_recommendation.rationale: AF-related thrombi are often more fibrin-rich and organized, potentially resisting thrombolysis compared to local atherosclerotic thrombi.

hypothesis.mechanism: Cardioembolic clots are often larger and have been formed longer before the event, making them less susceptible to tPA-mediated lysis.
evidence_basis: Cardioembolic stroke studies
Clot imaging studies
hypothesis.testable_prediction: Odds ratio for OHS 0-2 with treatment will be lower in atrialfib_rand == 1 compared to non-AF patients.
